proposed.label: Square bracket written next to infinity
proposed.description: The student treats infinity like an end number that can be included, so writes a square bracket next to it, as in $[-\infty, 5]$ or $[5, \infty]$. Infinity is not a number and always takes a round bracket.

proposed.label: Half-line written running the wrong way
proposed.description: The student writes the interval that starts at the end number and runs the opposite way along the number line, for example $[5, \infty)$ for $x \le 5$ or $(-\infty, 5]$ for $x \ge 5$, matching the bracket to the sign but mixing up which side of the number the set lies on.

distractors.text: $0 \le s \le 6$ m: the total distance the ball rolls down the slope

proposed.label: Reads the domain from the vertical axis
proposed.description: The learner gives the interval of the function values (the vertical axis) when asked for the domain, and so describes it as a distance instead of a time; domain and range are swapped.

distractors.text: $0 \le t \le 14$ s: the total time the ball takes to reach the bottom of the slope

proposed.label: Takes the drawn length of the axis as the domain or range
proposed.description: The learner reads the domain from how far the axis is drawn instead of from where the graph starts and stops, so gives an interval that is longer than the graph.

distractors.text: $0 \le t \le 12$ s: the distance the ball still has to roll

proposed.label: Right interval, meaning taken from the other variable
proposed.description: The learner finds the correct interval of input values but says it represents the quantity on the other axis (the distance still to roll) instead of the time taken.

proposed.label: Takes the number on the right of the equation as the $y$-intercept
proposed.description: Treats the constant in $ax+by=c$ as the $y$-intercept, as it would be in $y=mx+c$, instead of letting $x=0$ and solving $by=c$, so the division by the coefficient of $y$ is skipped.

proposed.label: Gives the range instead of the x-values where the graph rises or falls
proposed.description: The student answers with the y-values the graph takes (y ≥ q or y ≤ q) when asked for the values of x where it is increasing or decreasing.

proposed.label: Treats q as an x-value
proposed.description: The student thinks the turning point of y = ax^2 + q sits at x = q (reading it as (q, 0)), so they start the interval at x = q instead of x = 0. The constant q shifts the graph up or down, not left or right.

proposed.label: Chooses the wrong side of the turning point
proposed.description: The student picks x ≤ 0 where x ≥ 0 is right, or the reverse. Either they ignore the sign of a (assuming every parabola rises to the right of the turning point) or they mix up increasing and decreasing.

proposed.label: A shift up or down is applied the wrong way
proposed.description: The student moves the graph vertically in the wrong direction, down when it should go up and up when it should go down, so the sign of q, or of the change in q, is read backwards.

proposed.label: A negative a is treated as a small a
proposed.description: The student compares the values of a with their signs, so a negative a (for example -6) is taken as smaller than a positive a (for example 2), instead of comparing the sizes |a| to decide how far the graph lies from the axes.

distractors.text: The graph of $f$ is shifted 5 units to the right.

proposed.label: q is thought to shift the graph sideways
proposed.description: The student believes that changing the constant q moves the graph to the left or right instead of up or down.

distractors.text: The graph of $f$ is shifted 5 units down.

proposed.label: A shift up or down is applied the wrong way
proposed.description: The student moves the graph vertically in the wrong direction, down when it should go up and up when it should go down, so the sign of q, or of the change in q, is read backwards.

distractors.text: The graph of $f$ is shifted 3 units up.

proposed.label: The shift is read from the new q alone
proposed.description: The student takes the shift to be the value of q in the new equation and ignores the q that the first graph already had, instead of finding how much q has changed.

proposed.label: Placing the hyperbola's $y$-intercept at the origin
proposed.description: The student pictures the basic hyperbola as passing through or centred on the origin and gives $(0, 0)$ as the $y$-intercept, instead of noticing that $x=0$ makes the fraction undefined.

proposed.label: Reporting the $x$-intercept's value as the $y$-intercept
proposed.description: The student sets $y=0$, solves for $x$, and then writes that value as a point on the $y$-axis, $(0, x)$, so they confuse which variable is set to zero for which intercept.

distractors.text: The branches lie in the top-right and bottom-left regions formed by the asymptotes; the asymptotes are $x = 0$ and $y = -2$; the $x$-intercept is $(-\frac{5}{2}, 0)$.
The branches lie in the top-right and bottom-left regions formed by the asymptotes; the asymptotes are $x = 0$ and $y = 5$; the $x$-intercept is $(-\frac{5}{2}, 0)$.
The branches lie in the top-left and bottom-right regions formed by the asymptotes; the asymptotes are $x = 0$ and $y = 2$; the $x$-intercept is $(-\frac{5}{2}, 0)$.

proposed.label: Puts the branches in the wrong pair of regions for the sign of a
proposed.description: The student reads the sign of a wrongly, often through a slip when rewriting xy = a + qx as y = a/x + q, and so places the branches in the pair of regions that belongs to the opposite sign of a, even though the asymptotes and intercept are right.

proposed.label: Picks the rising graph with the smaller base for negative x
proposed.description: The student correctly sees that the order of the rising graphs reverses for negative x (b^x is above c^x there) but overlooks that both rising graphs are below 1 for negative x, so both decreasing graphs lie far above them.

proposed.label: Ranks the two decreasing graphs by the size of their bases
proposed.description: The student knows that at a negative x-value the decreasing graphs y = (1/b)^x and y = (1/c)^x lie above 1, but picks the one with the larger base (1/b is bigger than 1/c) instead of working out that at negative x the smaller base gives the larger y-value.

proposed.label: Thinks the graph with the largest base is the highest at every x
proposed.description: The student turns 'a larger base makes a steeper graph' into 'a larger base makes a higher graph' and picks y = c^x at a negative x-value, where it is in fact the lowest of the four graphs.

proposed.label: Includes y = q in the range
proposed.description: The student writes a square bracket, [q, infinity) or (-infinity, q], as if the graph reached the line y = q. It only gets closer and closer, so the bracket must be round.

proposed.label: Puts the range on the wrong side of y = q
proposed.description: The student gives (-infinity, q) when a is positive, or (q, infinity) when a is negative, instead of using the sign of a to decide whether the graph lies above or below y = q.

proposed.label: Ignores q: takes y = 0 as the boundary of the range
proposed.description: The student states the range of y = ab^x + q as (0, infinity) or (-infinity, 0), forgetting that q moves the boundary line from y = 0 to y = q.

proposed.label: Ignores q: takes y = 0 as the boundary of the range
proposed.description: The student states the range of y = ab^x + q as (0, infinity) or (-infinity, 0), forgetting that q moves the boundary line from y = 0 to y = q.

proposed.label: Puts the range on the wrong side of y = q
proposed.description: The student gives (-infinity, q) when a is positive, or (q, infinity) when a is negative, instead of using the sign of a to decide whether the graph lies above or below y = q.

proposed.label: Ignores the sign of a
proposed.description: The student uses q correctly but gives y = -ab^x + q the same range as y = ab^x + q, so the graph with a negative a is wrongly placed above y = q.

proposed.label: Ignores the sign of a
proposed.description: The student finds q correctly but says the range lies above y = q even though a is negative, so the graph lies below it.

proposed.label: Takes the y-coordinate of the given point as q
proposed.description: The student treats the y-value of the point on the graph as the value of q, forgetting that for y = ab^x + q the value of the function at that point is made up of ab^x as well as q.

proposed.label: Subtracts instead of adding when solving for q
proposed.description: From c = -P + q the student writes q = c - P instead of q = c + P, moving the term across the equals sign without changing its sign.

proposed.label: A positive a keeps the graph above the x-axis
proposed.description: Decides that a graph with a > 0 stays above the x-axis and so has no x-intercept, ignoring that a negative constant q shifts the graph down far enough to cross the axis.

proposed.label: b^x is never zero, so there is no x-intercept
proposed.description: Reasons that y = ab^x + q can never equal 0 because b^x is never 0, carrying the 'no x-intercept' of y = ab^x over to every exponential function and forgetting that q can cancel ab^x.

proposed.label: A negative a keeps the graph below the x-axis
proposed.description: Decides that a graph with a < 0 stays below the x-axis and so has no x-intercept, ignoring that a positive constant q shifts the graph up far enough to cross the axis.

distractors.text: It rises as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y=4$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, 5)$.
It rises as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y=4$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, -1)$.
It falls as $x$ increases, has the horizontal asymptote $y=4$ and cuts the $y$-axis at $(0, -5)$.

proposed.label: Takes the distance between the turning points as a
proposed.description: The student subtracts the lowest value from the highest value and uses the whole height, 2|a|, as the stretch factor instead of halving it to get the amplitude.

proposed.label: Gets the sign of a (the reflection) the wrong way round
proposed.description: The student finds |a| and q correctly but decides which turning point is the maximum the wrong way, so they write a positive a for a graph that is reflected in the x-axis, or a negative a for one that is not.

proposed.label: Gets the direction of the vertical shift wrong
proposed.description: The student finds the size of the shift but writes the opposite sign for q, so a graph shifted up is written as shifted down and the other way round.

proposed.label: Ignores the vertical shift q in the range
proposed.description: Gives -a <= f <= a, the range of a sin(theta), as if q = 0. The graph of a sin(theta) + q is the same graph moved q units up or down, so both ends of the range move by q.

proposed.label: Ignores the amplitude a in the range
proposed.description: Gives q - 1 <= f <= q + 1: shifts the range -1 <= sin(theta) <= 1 by q but forgets that a stretches it, so the distance from the middle line to the turning points is a, not 1.

proposed.label: Moves the range the wrong way
proposed.description: Gives -a - q <= f <= a - q: takes + q to mean a shift of q units in the opposite direction, so a positive q lowers the range and a negative q raises it.

proposed.label: Forgets the vertical shift q when stating the range
proposed.description: Gives the range of a cos θ, from -a to a, without moving it up or down by q.

proposed.label: Forgets the amplitude a when stating the range
proposed.description: Shifts the range of cos θ, from -1 to 1, by q but does not stretch it by the factor a.

proposed.label: Moves the range the wrong way for q
proposed.description: Subtracts q from both ends of the range of a cos θ, so a positive q moves the graph down and a negative q moves it up.

proposed.label: Getting the reflection in the x-axis the wrong way round
proposed.description: The student swaps the heights at 0 and 360 degrees with the height at 180 degrees: for a negative a they ignore the reflection and start the sketch at its maximum as for y = cos theta (and for a positive a they start it at its minimum), so the two turning heights q + a and q - a trade places.

proposed.label: Leaving out the vertical shift q
proposed.description: The student plots the points of y = a cos theta and forgets to add q, so the sketch is centred on the x-axis instead of on the line y = q.

proposed.label: Shifting the graph the wrong way
proposed.description: The student applies the shift with the wrong sign, subtracting q instead of adding it, so a graph shifted up is drawn shifted down and the other way round.

proposed.label: Takes the highest y-value as the vertical shift q
proposed.description: Reads q straight off the y-value of the highest point (the y-intercept), forgetting that this value is a + q and already contains the amplitude.

proposed.label: Takes the full height of the graph as a
proposed.description: Uses the whole distance from the lowest point to the highest point as the amplitude a, instead of half of it. The amplitude is measured from the middle line to the top (or bottom), not from the bottom to the top.

proposed.label: Swaps a and q
proposed.description: Finds the right two numbers but puts the shift in front of cos and the amplitude at the end, confusing which of a and q stretches the graph and which moves it up or down.

proposed.label: Believes cosine is sine shifted 90 degrees to the right
proposed.description: Uses cos(theta) = sin(theta - 90 degrees) instead of sin(theta + 90 degrees), so the 90 degrees is added to the other shift in the wrong direction.

proposed.label: Ignores that cosine is already a 90 degree shift of sine
proposed.description: Reads cos(x - p) as 'the graph of f shifted right by p', using the number inside the bracket as the whole shift and forgetting that the sine and cosine graphs are themselves 90 degrees apart.

proposed.label: Reverses the direction of the horizontal shift
proposed.description: Finds the right size of shift between the sine and cosine graphs but reads the sign the wrong way, so a leftward shift is reported as rightward (or the reverse).

proposed.label: Thinks the tangent graph always passes through the origin
proposed.description: Gives the y-intercept as (0, 0) because tan 0 = 0, forgetting that q shifts the whole graph so the y-intercept is (0, q).

proposed.label: Thinks the tangent graph repeats every 360 degrees
proposed.description: Uses the period of sine and cosine for the tangent graph, so gives a period of 360 degrees, or finds only one asymptote in a 360 degree interval instead of two.

proposed.label: Takes tan 0 degrees to be 1
proposed.description: Substitutes tan 0 degrees = 1 into a tan(theta) + q and gives the y-intercept as (0, a + q) instead of (0, q).

proposed.label: Leaves y = q out of the range
proposed.description: Carries over the hyperbola idea that the shift q is a horizontal asymptote that is never reached, so gives y in R, y not equal to q.

proposed.label: Gives the range of sine and cosine
proposed.description: States -1 <= y <= 1 for the tangent graph, ignoring both that tangent is unbounded and the effect of a and q.

proposed.label: Gives a tangent graph a bounded range using a as an amplitude
proposed.description: Treats a as an amplitude and q as the shift of the middle line, so gives the range q - |a| <= y <= q + |a| as for a sine or cosine graph.
